findings.summaryTemplate: Traffic between your browser and this server is encrypted over TLS.
findings.evidenceTemplate: The final page URL is served over HTTPS ({finalUrl}).
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Encryption prevents network eavesdroppers from intercepting your data or tampering with page content in transit.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Note that while HTTPS encrypts traffic, it does not verify whether the site's content or business is trustworthy.
findings.limitations: TLS encrypts transport but does not validate operator trustworthiness.

findings.summaryTemplate: This site communicates over plain, unencrypted HTTP.
findings.evidenceTemplate: The final page URL is unencrypted ({finalUrl}).
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Any information sent or received can be intercepted, read, or modified by anyone on the local network or internet path.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Avoid submitting credentials, personal details, or payment info on this site.
findings.limitations: Observed via primary HTTP request.

findings.titleTemplate: Sensitive Form Submits Insecurely or Cross-Origin
findings.summaryTemplate: A password input is submitted to an insecure destination or different domain.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Sending passwords over unencrypted HTTP or to third-party domains is a hallmark of credential harvesting and phishing.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Do not enter your credentials or account information on this page.
findings.limitations: Detected by parsing static form elements and action URLs.

findings.summaryTemplate: This page contains a password input field.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Legitimate login pages ask for passwords, but cloned phishing sites do too. Verify you are on the authentic domain.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Confirm the domain in your browser's address bar matches the exact service you intend to log into.
findings.limitations: Presence of a password field is normal on authentic login pages.

findings.summaryTemplate: No password input fields were detected in the page HTML.
findings.evidenceTemplate: No <input type="password"> tags found in static HTML.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: The page does not appear to solicit user account passwords.
findings.recommendationTemplate: None required.
findings.limitations: Dynamically rendered login forms injected by JavaScript post-load may not appear in initial static HTML.

findings.summaryTemplate: The page initiates an automatic redirect via an HTML meta tag.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Meta-refresh tags are frequently used in phishing landing pages to rapidly bounce users to credential harvest pages.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Ensure the redirect destination is legitimate and expected.
findings.limitations: Some legacy content sites use meta refresh for legitimate site migrations.

findings.summaryTemplate: The site instructs browsers to only connect over HTTPS in the future.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: HSTS protects users against SSL-stripping and man-in-the-middle downgrade attacks.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Maintain HSTS configuration with includeSubDomains and preload.
findings.limitations: Only active after initial browser visit establishes the trust pin.

findings.summaryTemplate: HSTS is present but has a short duration.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Short max-age durations reduce long-term protection against connection downgrades.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Consider extending HSTS max-age to at least 1 year (31,536,000 seconds).
findings.limitations: Sites in testing phase often use short max-age periods temporarily.

findings.summaryTemplate: The server does not send a Strict-Transport-Security header.
findings.evidenceTemplate: No Strict-Transport-Security header found in HTTP response.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Without HSTS, initial visits could be vulnerable to SSL-stripping on hostile networks (e.g. public Wi-Fi).
findings.recommendationTemplate: Enable HSTS on the origin web server.
findings.limitations: Applicable only to sites served over HTTPS.

findings.summaryTemplate: The site defines a Content Security Policy restricting resource execution.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: CSP helps prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), malicious script injection, and clickjacking.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Maintain strict CSP directives without 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' where possible.
findings.limitations: A CSP with permissive directives may still allow certain script injections.

findings.summaryTemplate: No Content-Security-Policy header was sent by the server.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: A CSP provides defense-in-depth against code injection and unauthorized framing.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Deploy a Content-Security-Policy header.
findings.limitations: Absence of CSP does not mean the site is compromised; it reflects absence of a defense-in-depth layer.

findings.summaryTemplate: X-Content-Type-Options is set to 'nosniff'.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Prevents browsers from MIME-sniffing a response away from the declared content-type, blocking script execution disguised as images or text.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Properly configured.
findings.limitations: Enforced by conforming modern browsers.

findings.summaryTemplate: The site controls whether it can be embedded inside iframes on other domains.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Prevents clickjacking attacks where a malicious site disguises the page inside an invisible frame.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Framing defense properly active.
findings.limitations: Verified on primary HTML response.

findings.summaryTemplate: Server banners disclose exact software version numbers.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Broadcasting exact software versions helps automated scanners look for known software vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Suppress granular version numbers in Server and X-Powered-By response headers.
findings.limitations: Information disclosure only; does not prove an exploitable vulnerability exists.

findings.summaryTemplate: Zero script tags were detected in the static HTML.
findings.evidenceTemplate: 0 script elements found in fetched document.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Fewer scripts reduce client-side attack surface and third-party tracking.
findings.recommendationTemplate: None required.
findings.limitations: Static inspection only; external scripts could be loaded if page were dynamically rendered by a service worker.

findings.summaryTemplate: The page loads {scriptCount} external scripts from {originCount} distinct domains.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Loading many external scripts increases supply chain risk, dependency on third parties, and tracking.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Review whether all included third-party scripts are essential.
findings.limitations: Complex single-page applications naturally use more scripts than simple static blogs.

findings.summaryTemplate: Detected dynamic code execution combined with string decoders (e.g. eval + atob/unescape).
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Malicious payloads frequently use runtime evaluation decoders to bypass static inspection.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Exercise extreme caution before executing scripts from this page.
findings.limitations: Some legitimate legacy packaging tools and copy-protection tools use unpackers.

findings.summaryTemplate: The page embeds {frameCount} iframe(s) from external origins.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Iframes can render external content. When unsandboxed, they may execute cross-domain widgets or ads.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Ensure embedded third-party sources are trusted.
findings.limitations: Third-party iframes are commonly used for benign widgets (YouTube, Google Maps).

findings.summaryTemplate: The page threw multiple unhandled JavaScript errors during loading.
findings.evidenceTemplate: Browser runtime observed {errorCount} unhandled client script errors.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Excessive client errors may indicate broken scripts or compatibility bugs.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Inspect browser console logs.
findings.limitations: Collected during passive headless navigation.

findings.titleTemplate: IP Address Used as Website Address
findings.summaryTemplate: The site is addressed directly via a numeric IP address rather than a registered domain name.
findings.evidenceTemplate: Target host is bare IP address: {host}.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Legitimate websites almost always use registered domain names. IP URLs are frequently used in targeted attacks to evade domain reputation filters.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Avoid submitting personal information to direct IP addresses.
findings.limitations: Some developer tools and internal staging servers use IP literals.

findings.summaryTemplate: The domain name exhibits patterns common in algorithmically generated domains.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Spammers and phishing campaigns often register bulk disposable domains with multiple hyphens or free TLDs.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Verify the domain carefully against the official company name.
findings.limitations: Heuristic observation; legitimate businesses occasionally use long hyphenated domains.

findings.summaryTemplate: The domain uses a standard top-level domain and natural length.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Domain structure conforms to typical human-selected naming conventions.
findings.recommendationTemplate: None required.
findings.limitations: Domain name appearance alone does not guarantee operator integrity.

findings.titleTemplate: Potential Brand Name in Unrelated Domain
findings.summaryTemplate: The domain name contains the well-known brand '{brand}' but is not registered to the official provider.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Phishing sites frequently embed authentic brand names into third-party subdomains or hyphenated domains to deceive users.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Confirm you are navigating to the official, verified web portal.
findings.limitations: Heuristic match based on brand catalog.

findings.summaryTemplate: The page text uses urgent pressure tactics or prize promises typical of scams.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Scams frequently manufacture artificial urgency or promise unrealistic rewards to induce hasty user action.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Do not follow instructions demanding immediate funds, gift cards, or credentials.
findings.limitations: Keyword matching in visible text; context should always be evaluated.

findings.summaryTemplate: We did not find aggressive pressure tactics or typical prize scam language.
findings.evidenceTemplate: Zero tracked high-pressure scam keyword phrases matched.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: The text does not show obvious automated scam indicators.
findings.recommendationTemplate: None required.
findings.limitations: Scammers continually vary phrase patterns; absence of known keywords is not proof of safety.

findings.summaryTemplate: The page contains terminology associated with {topic} services.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Helps contextualize what category of service this website offers.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Verify that this topic matches what you expected at this web address.
findings.limitations: Heuristic whole-word frequency match.

findings.summaryTemplate: The site links to a readable {kind}.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Available policies allow visitors to understand data collection, terms of use, and legal rights.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Review the policy if you plan to share sensitive or personal information.
findings.limitations: Automated text extraction does not substitute for formal legal review.

findings.titleTemplate: No Terms or Privacy Policy Found
findings.summaryTemplate: No links to a Terms of Service or Privacy Policy were detected on this page.
findings.evidenceTemplate: HTML links scan matched zero policy links.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Legitimate businesses and services publish policies explaining user rights, liability, and data practices.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Look for policies in the site footer or contact the website operator.
findings.limitations: Policies may be located on a separate landing domain or parent corporate site.

findings.summaryTemplate: The page links to a {kind}, but the destination could not be loaded.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Broken policy links prevent visitors from learning how their data is handled.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Verify whether the site operator maintains up-to-date policy documents.
findings.limitations: The policy server may have experienced temporary downtime.

findings.titleTemplate: Observed Tracking Not Clearly Disclosed in Policy
findings.summaryTemplate: External tracking scripts were observed, but the analyzed privacy policy does not explicitly mention cookies or advertising analytics.
findings.evidenceTemplate: Observed trackers ({trackers}) without explicit cookie/advertising disclosures in analyzed text.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Privacy regulations require sites to clearly disclose third-party tracking and analytics.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Check if cookie disclosures are located in a separate dedicated Cookie Policy.
findings.limitations: Disclosures may be located in an unlinked Cookie Policy or separate consent modal.

findings.summaryTemplate: The privacy policy contains explicit statements that user personal data is not sold or monetized.
findings.whyItMattersTemplate: Clear commitments against selling personal information provide affirmative privacy protections.
findings.recommendationTemplate: Review full policy for exceptions regarding service provider transfers.
findings.limitations: Reflects policy statements; scanner cannot independently audit internal corporate data practices.
